plot: Monday at sunset Mom tests her shop-window display on the dinner table and glazes old Bup with egg wash and sesame seeds, and jealous Lolly's one try to steal his cake stand lands her in the seed jar; then Mom turns over the old bakery sign Crispy warned them to leave face down, and the painted 1975 window loaf has Bup's big eye, small eye and stitch — Bup was the old bakery's window bread and remembers nothing, Lolly makes peace, and Crispy reveals Bup left because of a fire and that he wasn't the only bread in that window.

script.title: Why Is Bup's Face on the Old Bakery Sign?

beats.say: Help! She's painting me! Something sticky is on my head!
Hold still, Bup! Why would Mom put YOU in her shop window?
New episode every day. Subscribe so you don't miss what happens next.
Monday, sunset, the dinner table. Mom is testing her new shop window.
A cake stand. Dry wheat. Tiny lights. And in the middle… Bup.
She brushes egg wash on his crust. Shiny. Sticky. Very sticky.
Why him? He's lumpy. He's stale. I have actual sparkles!
Jealous, Lolly? Look at me. I glow. I'm basically famous.
Then Mom shakes a jar of sesame seeds. All over Bup's head.
I itch. I itch everywhere. Is this what being famous feels like?
Fact. Bakeries sell fresh bread. Bup is the opposite of fresh.
M-maybe she wants to scare the mice away with him?
Scare mice? Pim, he's the window star. I'm the decoration.
Mom leans an old wooden board against the wall. Face down.
It's the old bakery sign. She brought it home to repaint it.
Leave that sign alone. Some things are better left face down.
W-why? Is something scary painted on it? A face? Teeth?
Mom goes to the kitchen for her paint. The table goes quiet.
My turn. Window stars should sparkle. Watch and learn, crusty.
Lolly shoves Bup off the cake stand and climbs up herself.
Hey! Find your own cake stand, cookie!
But the stand wobbles. Lolly slides. Right into the sesame jar.
Don't. Say. Anything. Not one single word, Bup.
Mom's coming back! If she sees us moved, she'll know we're alive!
Bup jumps back on the stand. Lolly rolls under a napkin.
Mom sits down with her brush. Then she stops. And stares.
She's staring at you, Bup. Did you blink? Tell me no.
Mom turns the old sign over. Walter's Bakery, it says. Since 1975.
And under the words, there's a painted loaf of bread.
One big eye. One small eye. And a little stitched mouth.
Coincidence. Lots of bread is lumpy. Right? Right, Zeek?
One stitch. One big eye. One small eye. Odds of coincidence: zero.
S-so Bup is old? Like, really old? Fifty years old?
Bup. You are older than Mom. You are older than MOM.
Mom holds the sign up next to Bup. Same eyes. Same stitch.
Mom smiles. The old baker painted his window loaf, she says.
And this one looks just like it. Like it finally came home.
Came home? I don't remember any bakery. I don't remember anything.
Bup, if you lived in that window, why did you leave?
And if Mom puts you back there, you'll be alone again.
Th-then we all go in the window. As… decoration crumbs.
Mom finishes the sign and goes to wash her brush.
Bup. Sorry I pushed you. You're the real star. Seeds included.
Thanks, sparkles. But I'm not going anywhere without you four.
Then Crispy rolls out of the shadows. Slowly.
You left because of the fire, Bup. That night. I remember.
Crispy. How could you know? You weren't there. Were you?
You weren't the only bread in that window, old friend.
What do you think happens in the next part?
Tell me in the comments.
